title: Nidec Lays Out Recovery Plan With Unit Sales, Investments for AI
summary: Nidec Corp. pledged to sell off low-profit units such as household appliances and automotive motors while investing in its businesses for the AI, chips and energy sectors, seeking to restore investor trust after an accounting scandal wiped off a third of its value.

title: US Manufacturing Expansion Continues as Prices Jump
summary: US manufacturing activity expanded at a slightly slower pace in September as the Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing gauge fell 0.1 point to 54.5, according to data released Thursday. Factory activity has been in expansionary territory for nine consecutive months, the longest stretch since 2022. Michael McKee has the details on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Deal: Atlanta Braves Investor on Selling
summary: The Atlanta Braves are one of only a few publicly traded sports teams, which makes the argument for its sale a unique one in a year when two other MLB teams were sold at record valuations. On this episode of The Deal, Alex Rodriguez and Jason Kelly talk to the Founder and Portfolio Manager of Breach Inlet Capital Management, Chris Colvin about his sales pitch. Listen to their full conversation wherever you get your podcasts  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: M&A Slips 10% in Setback for Potential Record Year
summary: The value of announced deals in the three months through September dipped roughly 10% year-on-year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Michelle Davis reports on "Bloomberg The Open." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Rise of the 80/20 Portfolio Among ETF Investors
summary: In this episode of Trillions, we also look at data pointing to bipartisan investment tastes and why Septembers are lousy for markets.

title: Odd Lots: Why Are Global Bond and US Treasury Yields Rising?
summary: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Luke Kawa, head of markets at Sherwood News, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal to discuss how domestic and global growth impulse is driving a lot of the market moves that we're seeing, from persistent inflation to rising global bond and US Treasury yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall After Manufacturing Data as Oil Climbs: Markets Wrap
summary: A rally in oil prices sent stocks lower, with the market extending losses in the aftermath of a weaker-than-anticipated manufacturing report.

title: Bond Market’s Power Grows as Borrowing Costs Rise
summary:
Financial Times Alphaville editor and author of A Fabulous Debt Robin Wigglesworth tells Bloomberg This Weekend that rising bond yields reflect resilient growth and higher inflation expectations, but could increasingly constrain US spending as debt-service costs climb. Speaking with host David Gura, Wigglesworth explains why bonds underpin the global financial system and why today’s higher rates matter more in a heavily indebted economy. 

Interview occurred on September 26, 2026 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pakistan’s Fashion Brand Khaadi Plans IPO Next Month
summary: Khaadi Pakistan Ltd., a fashion retail company, is planning an initial public offering next month to fund its outlet expansion plan.

title: Australia Sees Global Commodity Woes Lifting Export Income by 5%
summary: Australia’s revenue from resource and energy exports is forecast to rise almost 5% in the year through June thanks to strong prices, even as its biggest trade partner China grapples with a years-long property crisis.

title: The Biggest Jump in Global Crop Prices Since 2022 Threatens to Boost Inflation
summary: Global agriculture prices notched their biggest quarterly jump since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, as tensions in the key Black Sea region and extreme weather threaten more inflationary worries for central banks.

title: Norway Fund Bought Tera-Run Turkey IPO That Plunged in Weeks
summary: Norway’s sovereign wealth fund was a key investor in an initial public offering underwritten by Tera Yatirim Menkul Degerler AS just two months before the brokerage firm became the center of the biggest fund scandal in Turkish history.

title: Chile’s Kast Finds More Room to Spend as Copper Revenue Surges
summary: Chile’s President José Antonio Kast plans to raise spending next year by more than originally envisaged as a windfall from record copper prices fills government coffers.

title: US Benchmark 10-Year Yield Briefly Hits Highest Since 2002
summary: The US benchmark yield touched its highest level since 2002, the latest milestone in a monthslong selloff in global sovereign debt.

title: Paramount’s $41 Billion of M&A Bonds Slump as Trading Begins
summary: Paramount Skydance Corp.’s $41 billion of US dollar bonds to finance its takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. sold off to start their first full day of trading while default-protection expenses surged to a 17-year high.

title: SK Hynix Mega-Listing Maintains US IPO Momentum in Third Quarter
summary: SK Hynix Inc.’s $26.5 billion US listing kept the streak of artificial intelligence-related mega-deals going in the third quarter, even as a trio of postponed smaller IPOs cast doubt on the market’s prospects aside from Anthropic PBC’s expected debut.

title: Miami Project Sells $1.7 Billion of Apartments Before It’s Built
summary: While condo sales across Miami have broadly slumped in recent years, one sector of the market is booming — ultra-luxury sales in apartments that haven’t even been built yet.

title: US Treasuries Appear Cheap Versus Stocks but May Have Further to Fall
summary: Treasuries might look cheap against stocks, GDP and the global cycle, but on their own historical terms they have more to fall before they become oversold and ready for a durable bounce.

title: US West Stays Warm After Second-Hottest September on Record
summary: Southern California and the West will start October much warmer than normal, after the US had its second-hottest September on record, according to a key metric used by energy traders and meteorologists.

title: US 10-Year Yield Hits 2002 High; Micron Gives Bullish Forecast
summary: The US 10-year yield hits its highest level since 2002 as rising oil prices fuel a renewed selloff in global bonds. US equity futures get support from chipmakers following an upbeat forecast from Micron. The results were driven by the AI building frenzy, but warned that rising compensation would weigh on profit margins. US companies announce the fewest number of job cuts for any September since 2022. Anastasia Amoroso of Partners Group joins "Bloomberg Brief" to discuss the bond selloff and the biggest risks to the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wei Li on AI Scarcity, Bond Selloff, Energy Price Shock
summary: Wei Li, BlackRock's Global Chief Investment Strategist said the release of new AI agents may "catalyze a wave of AI adoption". In an interview on "The Pulse with Francine Lacqua" on Wednesday September 30, Li also discussed the impact of the energy price shock, saying that the disruption to oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz is creating "macro damage", and that energy is a "big caveat" to their risk-on view.  (Source: Bloomberg)
